# Numerica Charitable Fund awards record $532,000 

The Numerica Charitable Fund fully funded every selected grant request this year, investing in programs that address the causes and effects of youth poverty.

 

## Investing in brighter futures, one grant at a time 

 Numerica Credit Union is making its largest Charitable Fund investment to date, awarding $532,000 to 23 nonprofits serving Eastern and Central Washington and North Idaho.

Charitable Fund recipient - Communities in Schools, June 2026

Charitable Fund recipient - Alexandria's House, June 2026

### This year marks a major milestone for the Numerica Charitable Fund. For the first time, every nonprofit selected received the full amount requested.

 The annual grant program supports nonprofits aligned with Numerica CARES for Kids, the credit union's philanthropic initiative addressing the causes and effects of youth poverty. Grants support prevention and intervention efforts that help vulnerable youth and families thrive.

Driven by a vision from Numerica President and CEO Carla Cicero to deepen the credit union's commitment to ending youth poverty, Numerica significantly expanded this year's funding to help nonprofits meet growing community needs.

"Through Numerica CARES for Kids, we are serious about ending youth poverty," said Carla Cicero, Numerica president and CEO. "This year, Numerica is investing more action and resources than ever before behind that commitment. These organizations are doing life-changing work every single day by helping families find housing, ensuring children have food to eat, creating educational supports and building brighter futures."

### Compared to last year's $372,000 investment, this year's funding increased by more than 40%.

"The need is greater than ever," Cicero said. "More families are struggling, more children need support, and many nonprofits are being asked to do more with less. We wanted to provide as much relief as possible by fully funding every selected grant request, giving these organizations the resources they need to continue changing lives."

The grants help fund critical services including food assistance, safe housing, education support, youth mentorship, crisis intervention and family stabilization programs.

## How the Numerica Charitable Fund works

The Numerica Charitable Fund is made possible through contributions from Numerica, its members and employees. Through the fund and Numerica CARES for Kids, the credit union partners with nonprofit organizations working to reduce the impacts of youth poverty and strengthen communities throughout the region.

It's one more way Numerica is working to enhance lives, fulfill dreams and build communities.

# 2025 Numerica Charitable Fund recipients 

Thanks to members and in partnership with Numerica CARES for Kids, $380,000 was distributed to 22 regional nonprofits through the 2025 Numerica Charitable Fund. 

### Investing in brighter futures, one grant at a time 

Across Spokane, Tri-Cities, North Idaho, and Wenatchee, kids are finding hope, support, and stability thanks to 22 nonprofits and the communities behind them. This year, Numerica’s Charitable Fund invested $380,000 into programs that do just that, including $100,000 in long-term partnerships. 

### A commitment to children and families 

Focused on kids. Powered by CARES. 

This year’s grants support organizations aligned with Numerica CARES for Kids, a philanthropic initiative focused on the well-being of children and families. This reflects the heart of Numerica: our commitment to supporting children and families across our region. 

As part of this effort, 4 nonprofits received their 3rd consecutive round of $25,000 in funding as part of Numerica’s multi-year pledge to help deepen their impact: 

- Family Promise of Spokane, Spokane
- Safe Passage, North Idaho
- Women’s Resource Center, Wenatchee
- Communities in Schools of Benton-Franklin, Tri-Cities 

These long-term partnerships make a lasting difference for local kids and Numerica is proud to walk alongside them every step of the way. 

“Numerica CARES for Kids is about investing in the well-being of children and families in our communities,” said Carla Cicero, Numerica president and CEO. “In challenging times, we’ve seen these 22 incredible nonprofits wrap their arms around those who need it most. Through the Numerica Charitable Fund, we’re honored to support the life-changing work they do every day.” 

### Distributing the grants 

Numerica team members surprised this year’s recipients with in-person grant announcements, along with Polaroid cameras to help capture “a day in the life of caring for kids.” These snapshots tell the story of what happens when a community comes together to lift others up. 

The $380,000 in grants supports a wide range of critical services, including: 

- Safe, stable housing
- Nutritious meals
- School supplies and learning tools
- Healing through trauma-informed care
- Enrichment and mentorship programs 

“Numerica CARES for Kids by helping create a safe, healing space for children who have been exploited,” said Tricia MacFarlan, executive director of Mirror Ministries. “Their support allows us to enhance the new Outreach Center and offer a warm, welcoming place for survivors to gather and heal.” 

### Meet the 2025 Numerica Charitable Fund recipients 

These organizations are stepping up for kids and families across Spokane, N Idaho and Central Washington.

# 22 Local nonprofits receive thousands from Numerica's youth-focused initiative 

- Kirstin O’Connor

 

#### Kirstin O’Connor 

Anchor

- Author facebook 
- Author twitter 
- Author email (koconnor@kxly.com)
- Aug 5, 2025 
- Aug 5, 2025 Updated Aug 5, 2025

 

 

 

SPOKANE VALLEY, Wash. — Numerica Credit Union just recognized 22 local nonprofits for their commitment to kids and families across the region with a $380,000 donation.

The money comes through Numerica's 2025 Charitable Fund and supports programs to end youth poverty, safe housing, child care, and educational support. 

The list of recipients in Spokane includes: Communities In Schools, Community-Minded Enterprises, Family Promise of Spokane, If You Could Save Just One, Partners with Families and Children, Second Harvest, Vanessa Behan, Volunteers of America, YMCA of the Inland Northwest and YWCA Spokane.

In North Idaho, three nonprofits also got support: 3rd Avenue Marketplace, Boys & Girls Club of Kootenai County and the Coeur d'Alene Backpack Program.

Four organizations are now in their third year of receiving substantial $100,000 multi-year grants. Family Promise of Spokane is one of them, along with Safe Passage in North Idaho, Women's Resource Center of North Central Washington in Wenatchee, and Communities In Schools of Benton-Franklin in the Tri-Cities.

“Numerica CARES for Kids is our commitment to ending youth poverty by supporting programs that create real, lasting change,” said Carla Cicero, Numerica president and CEO. “Through our Numerica Charitable Fund, we are proud to invest in organizations that care for the youth in our communities and reflect our core purpose of enhancing lives, fulfilling dreams and building stronger communities for generations to come.”

# $315,000 Granted to Nonprofits Through 2023 Numerica Charitable Fund

August 11, 2023

 

With grants for 19 regional nonprofits, Numerica Credit Union recently distributed more than $315,000 through the 2023 Numerica Charitable Fund.

The annual program partners with organizations that align with the credit union’s new philanthropic initiative, Numerica CARES for Kids.

As part of the announcement, the Spokane Valley, Washington-based Numerica also pledged $100,000 each to four nonprofits through multi-year grants.

- Family Promise, Spokane
- Safe Passage, North Idaho
- Women’s Resource Center, Wenatchee
- Communities in Schools of Benton-Franklin, Tri-Cities

These four-year commitments reflect special partnerships aimed at building brighter futures for local youth.

“Numerica CARES for Kids means focusing resources on organizations that uplift children and families,” said Carla Cicero, Numerica president and CEO. “When times are tough, we’ve seen how these 19 nonprofits wrap themselves around families in need. Through Numerica’s Charitable Fund we are proud to support organizations who are making an impact in the lives of others.”

Numerica team members surprised the nonprofits this summer with customized mini ATMs revealing the amount the organization was granted. The funds will be used to provide housing, meals, education, and more.

We couldn’t be more thankful!”

The Numerica Charitable Fund is funded by Numerica members through Skip a Pay, a voluntary program available on some loans. Members are allowed to bypass a monthly loan payment once every six months for a $30 fee, which is contributed to the fund to support community nonprofits.

# Numerica Charitable Fund 

 Through this initiative funded in part by members, grants are distributed to nonprofits serving Spokane, North Idaho, Tri-Cities, Moses Lake and the Wenatchee Valley. 

### Thank you to everyone who applied. Check back in early 2027 for the next application period.

### How the fund works

1. Numerica combines the generosity of members and employees with our corporate giving commitments.
2. These contributions build the annual Charitable Fund.
3. Charitable Fund grants are awarded to local nonprofits serving vulnerable youth and families.

### Grant process and amounts

Aligned with our Numerica CARES for Kids focus, the Numerica Charitable Fund prioritizes nonprofit applicants that positively impact vulnerable youth and families in terms of: 

- Educational success
- Financial stability
- Income and earning potential
- Crisis intervention and stabilization

### Info and eligibility

Charitable Fund grants support vulnerable youth and families located in Numerica’s service area. This includes Spokane, North Idaho, Tri-Cities, and Wenatchee Valley. Eligible* public, 501(c)(3) nonprofits are encouraged to apply for funds.

#### Numerica Charitable Fund grant requests are evaluated as part of a 2-step process:

1. Funding proposal
2. Application (by invitation)

The regional Charitable Fund grant committees will review all submitted proposals to assess which organizations will be invited to move to the full application phase. Please note that not all funding proposals will result in an invitation to submit a full grant application.

### These lead grant partners each received $100,000 pledges over four years to build brighter futures for local youth. 

To be eligible for a Numerica Charitable Fund grant, the organization must:

- Be a public, 501(c)(3) nonprofit
- Support vulnerable youth and families located in Numerica’s service area (Spokane, North Idaho, Tri-Cities, Moses Lake and Wenatchee Valley)

Please note the Numerica Charitable Fund does not award event sponsorships or funding for:

- Individuals or personal endeavors, schools, clubs, or teams
- Trips or tours
- Labor or fraternal organizations
- Churches
- Political or partisan groups

Requests for these can be made as a community sponsorship.

# Numerica Heroes Fund expands veteran support

The Numerica Heroes Fund is awarding $42,500 to local organizations supporting veterans, military families, and Gold Star Families.

![Heroes Fund Check Presentation 07 27 26 559x385](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/hero/Heroes-Fund-Check-Presentation-07.27.26-559x385.png?w=330&h=166&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1785249724&s=16eaac0b69d39989d8b53c5e34288e2a)![Heroes Fund Check Presentation 07 27 26 559x385](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/hero/Heroes-Fund-Check-Presentation-07.27.26-559x385.png?w=800&h=385&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1785249724&s=1f7c58e9c505547f8be1412584609e42)

## New grants strengthen veteran services

The Numerica Heroes Fund is expanding its support for veterans and military families by investing $42,500 in 3 local organizations that **strengthen mental health, honor fallen service members, and connect veterans and military families with critical community resources.**

Building on its [first investment](https://www.numericacu.com/news/numerica-heroes-fund) supporting housing for veterans experiencing homelessness, these grants continue the [Heroes Fund's $1 million, 10-year commitment](https://www.numericacu.com/news/spokane-arena) to those who have served.

### The latest grants include:

- $15,000 to [Veterans Community Response](https://www.vetcomres.org/) for veteran mental health and trauma recovery programs.
- $15,000 to [Washington State Fallen Heroes Project](https://www.wafhp.org/) to support Gold Star Families through remembrance, grief support, and community events.
- $12,500 to [Spokane County Regional Veteran Services](https://www.spokanecounty.gov/1122/Veteran-Services) to expand this October's Stand Down for Veterans at Numerica Veterans Arena.

## Supporting veteran mental health

Veterans Community Response hosts two annual retreats that help combat veterans reconnect, heal, and build lasting relationships through peer support, outdoor experiences, and guidance from trauma clinicians. **The Heroes Fund grant will keep the retreats free for participants while expanding access to mental health programming and peer connection.**

**"Your support strengthens our ability to reach veterans across the Inland Northwest and North Idaho, bringing them together in community, connection, and healing,"** said Terri Fowler of Veterans Community Response.

## Honoring fallen service members

The Washington State Fallen Heroes Project preserves the legacy of Washington's fallen service members while **supporting Gold Star Families through memorials, remembrance events, and community education.** The grant will help sustain those programs and continue bringing families, veterans, and the community together to honor those who made the ultimate sacrifice.

**"Every fallen hero deserves to be remembered by name, every Gold Star family deserves enduring support, and every community has a role in preserving that legacy,"** said Keirsten Lyons of Washington State Fallen Heroes Project.

## Expanding access to community resources

The Numerica Heroes Fund is also helping expand the annual **Stand Down for Veterans,** which moves to [Numerica Veterans Arena](https://www.numericacu.com/news/spokane-arena) this October. Hosted by Spokane County Regional Veteran Services, the event connects veterans and their families with healthcare, legal assistance, housing resources, employment services, meals, and other essential services.

## Looking ahead

Looking ahead, Numerica's Eastern Washington University football partnerships, including **Tailgate for a Cause** and **Touchdowns for a Cause**, will support military families with children through a new **partnership with Michael Anderson Elementary** and other local organizations.

Together, these investments continue the Numerica Heroes Fund's commitment to supporting veterans and military families through meaningful partnerships that strengthen lives and communities.

_Written July 2026_

_Written by Numerica’s Community Impact and Communications Team: Helping members grow their money across Spokane, North Idaho, Wenatchee, Moses Lake and the Tri-Cities._

A checking account is your **home to cash checks, set up a direct deposit from your job, and pay bills**. As a cornerstone to your financial well-being, it’s often the first account people open after breaking up with their piggy bank. (And you thought people who didn’t like piggy banks were afraid of _change_!)

Right now, you are probably afraid of more bad jokes. Let’s get to your checking account questions.

## How do I open a Numerica checking account?

Our team is ready to assist you! Whether you want to hop on a call, schedule an appointment, or locate your nearest branch, [**let's get started**](https://www.numericacu.com/connect).

### Can I open a Numerica checking account online?

Yes, if you are a new member you can [**start your application**](https://www.numericacu.com/apply?account=bonus_checking) now.

* * *

## Why should I open a checking account?

A checking account is a **convenient, secure way to access your money**. At Numerica, we are all about helping you live well financially. We make it easy to use your checking account to keep your money organized and protected. **Our accounts are federally insured by NCUA**.

* * *

## Where’s the checking account routing number?

Numerica’s routing number is **325182690**. This nine-digit code works like an ID number for your financial institution.

If you have checks, Numerica's routing number is the **first series of numbers on your check**.

![](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/Check-Routing-In-story-Numerica.png?w=550&h=252&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1727110823&s=a4795a7ad8a7487e33d0c19e10bbc1f1)

* * *

## Where's the checking account number on my check?

The **second series of numbers on your check is your account number.**

The set of numbers right after that is your check number and should be the same as the number in the upper right-hand corner of the check.

![](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/Check-Account-Number-in-story-Numerica.png?w=550&h=252&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1727110823&s=350c3a44b4aa62b8b01e8b48f3bb989a)

Taken all together, the three numbers across the bottom of a check communicate:

1. The financial institution the check will be cleared by
2. The specific account the money will be taken from, and
3. The check number used to identify the transaction

* * *

## How do I find my checking account number online?

- First, log in to either [**Online Banking**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/online-banking) or the [**Mobile App**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/mobile-app).

- Choose **Accounts**, and then select the specific account you want to view.


Your **full account number** will be listed near your available balance. (It will be listed as your **ACH number**.) If the number is concealed, **tap the eye icon to reveal it.**

* * *

## What’s the easiest way to see my checking account balance?

See your account balance on our [**Mobile App**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/mobile-app) or in [**Online Banking**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/online-banking).

* * *

## How do I order checks?

We will help you order your initial checks when you set up your checking account. Ready to reorder?

1. Log in to [**Online Banking**](https://digital.numericacu.com/). Note: This option is not available in the Mobile App
2. Click on **More** in the top menu
3. Click on **Reorder checks**
4. Select the appropriate account
5. Click **Place checkbook order**
6. Our check vendor’s site will open in your browser. Follow the prompts to select and order your new checks.

If your **name or address has changed, this should be updated before ordering new checks**. Call [**800.433.1837**](tel:8004331837) or stop by a [**Numerica branch**](https://www.numericacu.com/branches) to update your account information.

* * *

## When are my funds available after a deposit?

Numerica is committed to both the security and accessibility of your money. As we process deposits, we take care to follow all regulations and best practices.

**When do these funds become available in your account?** That depends on several factors, including:

- The type of check
- The amount of the check deposit
- The length and history of your account

Numerica’s Funds Availability Policy Disclosure is a great resource for reviewing timetables and scenarios. A copy is provided when you open an account, or you can request a copy anytime.

Of course, if you have a funds availability question specific to your account, we’re here to help. [**Reach out to us**](https://www.numericacu.com/contact).

* * *

## Does opening a checking account affect your credit score?

No. Your credit report only tracks your credit and debt.

Additionally, your checking account isn’t impacted by a low credit score. However, bad credit could impact your loan rates if you need a car, credit card, or if you decide to buy a home. It’s always a good idea to find ways to [**improve your credit**](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/credit-scores-interest-rates/).

Your ChexSystems record, on the other hand, **could impact your checking account**. ChexSystems identifies people who present a risk because of mishandling funds. If you’ve written a series of checks with non-sufficient funds (NSF), this isn’t reported on your credit score, but it could be reported to ChexSystems.

A poor ChexSystems report doesn’t necessarily mean you can’t open a Numerica account. At Numerica, our priority is your financial well-being. We offer a variety of options to help members build successful checking accounts — as well as establish or rebuild credit.

## What happens when my checking account goes negative?

We get it. Life moves — sometimes a bit too quickly — and the funds you expect to be in your account may not be.

A checking account that goes negative triggers overdraft fees. While the best way to [**avoid overdraft fees**](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/avoid-overdraft-fees/) is to limit your risk of insufficient funds, many financial institutions offer overdraft protection options. Call [**800.433.1837**](tel:8004331837) to discuss options for Numerica accounts.

## How do I know which checking account is the best choice for me?

Numerica has [**two checking accounts**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/checking): Free Checking and Bonus Checking. Both accounts let you [**customize your debit card**](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/debit-cards) and are free with eStatements. (See [**Fee Schedule**](https://www-files.numericacu.com/production/documents/olb-personal-fee-schedule-member.pdf?dm=1782489386).)

[![](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/landing-pages/transparent-affinity-cards-Numerica.png?w=450&h=310&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1770390713&s=488c62c2bda8f8e33242940605ad94ff)](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/debit-cards)

## Can a personal checking account be used for business?

On the surface, this may seem like an easy solution, but it’s a definite no-no. **Using your personal account for your business transactions can affect your legal liability.**

As soon as you register your new business, you should open an account specifically for it — even if it’s a home business or side-hustle.

Since businesses come in all shapes and sizes, Numerica has a diverse line of products to serve them, including several [**business checking**](https://www.numericacu.com/business/business-checking) account options. We can match your business needs to the right products. Visit a [**nearby branch**](https://www.numericacu.com/branches) to open your account today.

## How do I get my debit card for my checking account?

When you opened your checking account, you should have received a debit card either in the mail or at the branch. (If you haven't received one within one week, please [contact us](https://www.numericacu.com/contact) so we can ensure it's on its way to the correct address).

If you have misplaced your debit card, you can activate [**Card Freeze**](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/credit-card-freeze/) in the Mobile App or Online Banking until you can find it or replace it with a new card.

### Mobile:

1. Log in and tap **Cards** in the bottom menu.
2. Tap the **Active** toggle button of the card you want to freeze.
3. Confirm you’d like to freeze the card.
4. Un-freeze your card the same way.

### Online Banking:

1. Log in and select **Cards** from the top menu.
2. Click the **Active** toggle button of the card you want to freeze.
3. Confirm you’d like to freeze the card.
4. Un-freeze your card the same way.

If you believe your card is lost or stolen, please contact us immediately at [**800.433.1837**](tel:8004331837) so we can permanently block the card and send you a new card with a new number.

**Have you heard the one about the person who opened a checking account?**

**Representative:** Would you like a savings account, too?

**Person:** No, thank you.

**Representative:** OK, just _checking_.

What accounts are best for you? Let’s talk! Call [**800.433.1837**](tel:8004331837) or stop by [**your favorite Numerica branch**](https://www.numericacu.com/branches) today.

# POV: You're finally maxxing your savings

Want to earn more on the money you're already saving? That's what savings maxxing is all about.

![Article account faq Numerica 2](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/article-account-faq-Numerica-2.png?w=330&h=166&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1732219202&s=7442dcc7f0772132371da765d45ab321)![Article account faq Numerica 2](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/article-account-faq-Numerica-2.png?w=800&h=385&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1732219202&s=caad70a701539cad9cbcc9c0e91f7bc1)

## Savings maxxing starts here

Most people keep all their savings in one account. It's simple, but it can mean missing out on higher earnings, mixing emergency money with vacation savings, or leaving long-term savings in an account that's built for everyday access.

**Savings maxxing is about giving each dollar a job.** Instead of relying on one account to do everything, you **use different accounts for different goals.** Your money can earn more while staying available when you need it.

If "maxxing" sounds like a word your teenager invented, you're not alone. **It simply means getting the most out of something.** When it comes to your money, we're all for that.

### Is this the right strategy for you?

This approach works well if you're building savings over time and like having separate buckets for different goals.

**It may not be the best fit if you:**

- Need frequent access to all your savings
- Prefer keeping everything in a single account for simplicity
- Aren't able to consistently set money aside each month

If saving every month isn't realistic right now, focus on building a small emergency fund first. Once saving becomes part of your routine, you can expand your strategy over time.

### A simple savings strategy

**Think of it like this:**

- **Step 1:** Earn 6.00%\\* when you save your first $700 in [Six7 Savings](https://www.numericacu.com/six7)\*\*
- **Step 2:** Continue building your emergency fund or another savings goal with [Bonus Saver](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/bonus-saver-faqs)
- **Step 3:** Earn interest on the money you keep in [Bonus Checking](https://www.numericacu.com/300) for everyday spending
- **Step 4:** Once you've built your emergency fund, move money you won't need for several months into [certificates](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/certificates) to earn a competitive fixed rate

Not everyone's savings journey will look the same, and that's okay. The goal is simply to match the right account to the right purpose.

Quick tip: [Explore our guide on "Smart ways to save"](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/smart-ways-to-save-at-numerica)

## Step 1: Build your first savings milestone with SIX7 Savings

Start by building your savings. [Six7 Savings](https://www.numericacu.com/six7) helps your first $700 grow faster by earning 6.00% APY\\* on balances up to $700. APY means annual percentage yield.

Whether you're creating your first emergency fund or saving for [holiday shopping](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/beat-holiday-stress), car repairs, or another short-term goal, this account gives your dollars a powerful boost.

**Maxxing tip:** Turn on [Round Up to Savings](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/round-up-savings). Every time you make a purchase with your Numerica debit card, we'll round it up to the next dollar and automatically deposit the difference into your Six7 Savings account. It's an easy way to grow your savings without thinking about it.

**Once you've reached $700, you're ready for the next step.**

## Step 2: Grow your emergency fund with Bonus Saver

Once your Six7 Savings account reaches $700, keep the momentum going.

[Bonus Saver](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/bonus-saver-faqs) rewards consistency by earning 2.05% APY\\*\\* on balances up to $2,500 when you deposit at least $25 each month and make no withdrawals for 6 consecutive months.

It's a great place to continue building your emergency fund or save toward a larger goal.

**Quick Tip:** [DreamUp](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/dreamup) is a handy Numerica tool for automating your savings and tracking your progress.

**Maxxing Tip:** Once your Six7 Savings account reaches $700, direct your [Round Up](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/round-up-savings) deposits into your Bonus Saver account. This keeps your savings growing automatically while helping you stay on track to earn the bonus rate.

If you need to tap into your savings, consider using funds from your Six7 Savings account first so you can continue working toward your Bonus Saver qualifications.

## Step 3: Make your everyday money work harder

Your checking account doesn't have to sit idle. With a qualifying [Bonus Checking](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/bonus-checking-faqs) account\*\*\*, the **money you use for everyday expenses can also earn interest while remaining available** whenever you need it.

**Earn 2.00% APY\\* on balances up to $25,000 by:**

- Making at least 12 Numerica debit or credit card purchases of $5 or more each month
- Enrolling in [eStatements](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/estatements)

If you're already using your Numerica cards for everyday purchases, you may already be doing most of the work.

**Maxxing Tip:** Use your Numerica [debit](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/debit-cards) or [credit card](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/visa-cards) to **pay recurring expenses** like streaming services, utilities, insurance, and phone bills to help **meet your monthly transaction requirements**.

## Step 4: Put long-term savings to work with certificates

Once you've built your emergency fund and have money you don't plan to use for several months or longer, [certificates](https://www.numericacu.com/personal/certificates) can help you earn even more. Choose a term from 3 to 60 months and **lock in a competitive rate on deposits of $1,000 or more**.

**Maxxing Tip:** Consider **certificate laddering**. Instead of putting all your savings into one certificate, split it among several certificates with different maturity dates such as 6, 12, and 18 months. As each certificate matures, you can use the money if you need it or reinvest it, giving you access to portions of your savings while continuing to earn competitive rates.

## Put your savings strategy to work

**Savings maxxing isn't about opening every account just because you can**. It's about [matching the right account](https://www.numericacu.com/articles/right-savings-account) to the right goal.

Your everyday spending, emergency savings, and long-term savings all have different jobs. When each has the right home, your money can work harder without making your finances more complicated.

Whether you're saving your first $100 or looking to earn more on the money you've already saved, we're here to help you build a strategy that fits your goals.

### **Ready to build your savings strategy?**

Visit a [branch](https://www.numericacu.com/branches), [make an appointment](https://schedule.numericacu.com/ApptBookingTool/), or chat with us online to get started.

# Schedule an appointment with Numerica

Need assistance at your nearby Numerica branch?  In a few clicks, you can schedule an appointment for a time that’s convenient for you.

![Article account faq Numerica 2](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/article-account-faq-Numerica-2.png?w=330&h=166&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1732219202&s=7442dcc7f0772132371da765d45ab321)![Article account faq Numerica 2](https://www-images.numericacu.com/production/images/articles-and-news/article-account-faq-Numerica-2.png?w=800&h=385&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=clip&dm=1732219202&s=caad70a701539cad9cbcc9c0e91f7bc1)

## Waiting in line is never fun

### Instead, schedule an appointment with your favorite Numerica branch.

Whether you want to meet in person or over the phone, it’s easy to book a time that works for you.

[BOOK AN APPOINTMENT](https://schedule.numericacu.com/ApptBookingTool/)

### What kinds of services can I book an appointment for?

#### Book an appointment for anything that might take a little more time, like:

- Applying for a loan
- Opening a new account
- Setting up automatic payments
- Adding someone to your account
- Getting help with account or card issues
- Talking through your financial goals

## How to schedule your visit

### Step 1: Go to the [appointment scheduling tool](https://schedule.numericacu.com/ApptBookingTool/)

### Step 2: Select your service

Tell us **what you'd like to discuss during your appointment** to help us prepare to serve you. We’ll also let you know whether to bring specific documentation.

### Step 3: Choose your preferred language

Options include **English and Español**.

### Step 4: Pick where you’d like to meet

Select the Numerica [branch](https://www.numericacu.com/branches) location most convenient for you.

### Step 5: Select a date and time

Pick from the available morning or afternoon time slots.

### Step 6: Enter your info

We’ll need your name and contact information to confirm the appointment and send reminders.

### Step 7: You’re booked

You’ll get a confirmation email with your appointment details.

### How do I cancel or reschedule?

No problem. Cancel or reschedule right from your confirmation email or by calling us at [800.433.1837](tel:8004331837). Then, come back whenever you’re ready.

### Not ready to schedule? That’s okay, too

#### You don’t have to make an appointment to visit a branch. You can:

# Reasons to work at a credit union 

Discover fulfilling career opportunities at Numerica. Learn about the benefits, community involvement, and growth potential of working for credit unions.

Question: Where can you find the kind of job where your employer respects you, your family life, and your community?

Answer: Credit unions. (Trust us. We’re kind of an expert on this one.)

Credit unions are a fun and fulfilling place to work. Best of all, we make a difference in our members’ lives.

One way we do this at Numerica is by giving back to the communities we’re in: the greater Spokane, Tri-Cities, the Wenatchee Valley, and North Idaho areas.

But there’s much more, so let’s get to it! Here’s the nitty gritty of working for a credit union.

### Should I work for a credit union?

Absolutely! Credit unions are member-owned and not-for-profit. At Numerica, for example, our entire vibe is member-centric. We’re always working to give members lower fees, lower rates on loans, and higher interest on deposit accounts. (Maybe it’s just us, but that’s more fun than trying to rake in extra bucks for shareholders.)

When you work for Numerica, you are both an employee and a member. This means we care about your well-being in the same way we do our membership. We like to be consistent that way.

Numerica employees are empowered to make decisions, and there are opportunities for advancement and development. Numerica supports employees’ individual career paths to help them advance within the organization.

“The fact that my voice is actually being heard and things are happening because of it really does set this company apart from all other companies I’ve worked for,” said Sidney Lorentz, network and systems administrator.

### How are Numerica and other credit unions active in the community?

Credit unions give back to the communities they are in by supporting local charities, nonprofits, and community events. You’ll even see us team up together for causes like the Children’s Miracle Network.

This is in our DNA. Numerica is committed to giving back at least 5 percent of its earnings each year. We do this through community giving, scholarships, and innovative programs like the Numerica Charitable Fund, which is funded through the credit union’s Skip a Pay program.

But credit unions are about more than check writing. At Numerica, we believe in getting out and lending a hand. To show support for employees who want to do more to help their community, Numerica offers 8 hours of paid volunteer time annually. We even have a donation matching program.

There is never a lack of volunteer opportunities through sponsorships and nonprofit partners.

### Fostering financial education

Remember, we’re about our members and communities, so credit unions are big on financial education. We’re in the schools, in the community, and even in our own buildings teaching students, members, and employees how to budget, manage finances, and live well.

Numerica’s internal financial education program includes a treasure chest of tips and tools designed to promote employee well-being. Just another great reason to work here!

Numerica’s commitment to enhancing lives, fulfilling dreams, and building communities starts with a promise to our members and staff to help them live well financially. We know that every member’s financial journey is unique, but we also know that a strong relationship with money starts with simple conversations around topics like budgeting, saving, and credit.

Numerica’s Financial Education program is committed to supporting those conversations by becoming the dominant voice in how our members and our community can truly live well. From the classroom to the boardroom, Numerica is with you every step of the way.

### What kind of jobs are available at credit unions?

When visitors stop by or students tour our facilities, they are often surprised by the variety of positions available at credit unions, from entry-level service representative positions to leadership and managerial roles.

There are many departments that offer employment opportunities, such as human resources, organizational development, learning and design, IT, finance, member services, and marketing/communications. Jobs are available in all of the areas we serve.

Just a few examples of openings at Numerica include positions like network and systems administrator, business banking relationship officer, financial advisor, branch manager, and cash management representative.

Openings are constantly being posted as opportunities present themselves, so bookmark the Numerica careers page and check back frequently. As you view current openings, you can even set up a custom job alert to make sure you never miss that perfect opportunity. 

### What are the benefits of working at Numerica Credit Union?

There are so many benefits to working at Numerica! Some of the benefits and perks (yep, they are two different things) include:

- Tuition reimbursement
- Internal development opportunities
- Family day (paid day off plus $50)
- Wellness programs
- Employee referral program ($300 if you refer an awesome person)
- Personal time off
- 401(k) plan including employer match
- Employer-paid medical and dental benefits
- Maternity and paternity leave through the Family and Medical Leave Act

At this point, it’s starting to feel a little like bragging, but hey, Numerica is a boast-worthy place.

Just ask Jeff Escalera, our Richland branch manager.

“Numerica is all about family and community,” he said. “This was what attracted me to Numerica for my financial needs even before I worked here. The dedication Numerica shows to enhancing our community and how much they value us as employees allows me to give everything I have to my family and my community; I don’t have to choose. We are encouraged to volunteer in any and all events that drive us as individuals which contributes to a diverse and inclusive environment. I could not be more proud of the people and the organization I work with every day.”

### What kind of people does Numerica look for to fill positions?

First and foremost, Numerica looks for someone who is passionate about our core purpose of enhancing lives, fulfilling dreams, and building communities. If you’re fun, open to change, transparent, and work well on a team, then you should fit in nicely. Someone who wants to learn, grow, and has a passion for giving back to the community would feel right at home at Numerica.

Sometimes, seeing is believing, so we put together a video, The Numerica Experience, to give you a glimpse of what Numerica employees say about our special culture.

### What type of training and development is offered to those who work for Numerica?

New employees at Numerica go through a welcome and onboarding program that sets them up with all the tools necessary for a successful start.

From that first day on, we invest time, talent, and energy into personal and professional development. Our organizational development and learning and design teams offer a suite of internal courses ranging from leadership to technical training classes. These classes ensure all employees have the ability to continue to grow and develop both at work and at home.

### What is the application process at Numerica?

Numerica tries to make managing finances as easy as possible for its members, and employees receive the same treatment. Applying is simple, online process. Here’s what to expect:

- Numerica looks at your experiences based on the needs of the position.
- If you meet the requirements, you’ll be personally contacted within two to three weeks to schedule an interview.
- Human Resources conducts the first interview.
- Credit and criminal background checks are completed.
- If applicable, a teller test is administered.
- The hiring manager conducts a second round of interviews.
- Your application will remain in an active file for 60 days.

### What are you waiting for?

OK, let’s review:

- Credit unions are member-centric, community-minded places to work.
- Numerica is interested in investing in its employees to help them live well.
- While working at a credit union, you improve the well-being of your friends and neighbors
- You know how to find jobs and apply at Numerica.

We hope to see your application soon!

# 2022 International Credit Union Day 

Local credit unions partner with Habitat for Humanity, helping two families achieve their dream of homeownership through volunteer support and affordable housing.

 

October 17, 2022

SPOKANE — Two families will soon purchase their new homes in East Central Spokane in partnership with Habitat for Humanity and volunteer support from 19 local credit unions. Taking steps to address the housing crisis, hundreds of credit union volunteers have been working together the past month to make this project possible.

Nathan and Jessica Thomas will be moving into one of the homes with their children. Nathan, a military veteran, needed a home that is ADA accessible. The Thomases never thought owning a home would be possible.

“There’s a light at the end of the tunnel for us,” Jessica Thomas said. “We have two young kids and owning a home has been a dream our entire marriage. Thank you to all the volunteers for choosing to use their valuable time this way.”

The two homes are expected to be ready this winter. Kelsey McCarthy, a single mother with three children, will be moving into the second home.

“Without this program, I would never be able to purchase a house, especially right now,” Kelsey McCarthy said. “This is a blessing and I love seeing everyone come out for me and my family.”

Habitat for Humanity brings people together to build homes, communities and hope by helping families build and improve places to call home. Qualified homebuyers, earning below 80% of the area median income, help build their own homes alongside volunteers and pay an affordable mortgage.

“The partnership with our area credit unions highlights how affordable housing plays a critical role in strong and stable communities,” said Michelle Girardot, Habitat for Humanity-Spokane CEO. “By these volunteers lifting their hearts and hammers, two families will open the doors to a future to economic mobility and stability.”

The cooperative effort among local credit unions honors International Credit Union Day. For seven years, local credit union volunteers have worked side by side on community projects, united in a desire to show up and give back. Debie Keesee helped organize this year’s project as a member of the International Credit Union Day committee.

“The chance to do a project that involves up to 600 volunteer opportunities really drives home the credit union philosophy of people helping people,” said Keesee, president and CEO of Spokane Media Federal Credit Union. “All 19 credit unions coming together cooperatively enables two deserving families to meet Habitat for Humanity’s vision that everyone needs a decent place to live.”

This year’s participating credit unions include: Alaska USA Credit Union, Avista Credit Union, BECU, Canopy Credit Union, Cheney Federal Credit Union, Gesa Credit Union, Global Credit Union, Horizon Credit Union, Idaho Central Credit Union, Numerica Credit Union, PrimeSource Credit Union, Progressions Credit Union, Responders Emergency Services Credit Union, Safeway Employees Federal Credit Union, Spokane City Credit Union, Spokane Firefighters Credit Union, Spokane Media Federal Credit Union, STCU and WSECU.

# MoneyIRL gives Spokane students real-world money practice 

More than 1,000 high school students took part in MoneyIRL, a hands-on financial education event in Spokane.

 

September 2026

More than 1,000 Spokane-area high school students from 12 school districts gathered at the Spokane Convention Center for MoneyIRL, a hands-on financial education event hosted by Numerica Credit Union, Gesa Credit Union, STCU, and BECU.

## MoneyIRL at a glance

- 1,000+ high school students
- 12 Spokane-area school districts
- 4 credit unions working together
- A hands-on experience focused on real-world financial decisions

The event gave students a look at the kinds of financial decisions they may face as they complete high school and begin adulthood. Instead of just talking about budgets, students made decisions and saw how those choices affected their bottom line.

## Students made the decisions

One of the main activities was the Bite of Reality® simulation.

Students were given a fictional career, income, and family situation. Then they had to build a monthly budget that covered expenses such as:

- Housing
- Transportation
- Food
- Utilities

Unexpected costs were also built into the simulation. Students had to adjust their budgets and make choices about where their money went. Optional challenges gave them even more opportunities to test what they learned.

### Additional learning activities for students included:

- Cashy interactive investing experience 
- Money Trivia
- Credit Score PLINKO
- Dice of Life 

It was a different way to learn about money. Students weren’t just hearing about financial decisions. They were making them.

## A day of learning and inspiration 

MoneyIRL welcomed author and podcast host Blue Stiley, who kicked off the event with a keynote presentation that included humor, storytelling, and practical takeaways for students. 

Student engagement was rewarded with the chance to take home one of more than 50 prizes, ranging from gift cards to Meta glasses to a Nintendo Switch. 

## Credit unions worked together

MoneyIRL also brought 4 Washington credit unions together around a shared goal: helping more young people build the skills and confidence to manage money. Volunteers from several additional local credit unions also played an important role in bringing the event to life and supporting participants throughout the day.

The collaboration reflected the credit union principle of “ Cooperation Among Cooperatives,” bringing together the organizations’ resources and financial education experience to reach students across the Spokane region. 

“Students can learn the basics of budgeting, saving and credit, but putting those lessons into practice is different,” said Carla Cicero, president and CEO of Numerica Credit Union. “MoneyIRL gave students a chance to make those decisions in a low-stakes setting, before they’re making them on their own. We’re proud to have been part of this effort and to work alongside other credit unions to help students prepare for what comes next.” 

## Helping students build their financial futures

Financial education is one way Numerica supports young people as they prepare for life after high school. The credit union also supports students through scholarships and other opportunities that help make their next steps possible.

MoneyIRL brought those efforts together in a different way. Students had a chance to practice making financial decisions and see how those decisions could add up over time.

For Numerica, that’s an important part of helping young people prepare for what’s ahead.

Written September 2026

Written by Numerica’s Community Impact and Communications Team: Helping members grow their money across Spokane, North Idaho, Wenatchee, Moses Lake and the Tri-Cities.

### WHAT IS MONEYIRL?

MoneyIRL is a hands-on financial education event where high school students practice making real-world money decisions through simulations and interactive activities. 

### WHAT DID STUDENTS DO AT MONEYIRL?

Students worked through fictional income, family, and expense scenarios. They made decisions about housing, transportation, food, utilities, and other costs while trying to keep their monthly budgets on track. 

### WHAT IS BITE OF REALITY?

Bite of Reality is an interactive financial simulation that gives students a fictional financial situation and asks them to make everyday spending decisions. Their choices affect their budgets in real time. 

### DOES NUMERICA OFFER OTHER OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS?

Yes. Numerica supports students through financial education, its $tarting Off Right Scholarships, and other community programs focused on young people and families.

# Resources to help when money feels tight 

Find food assistance, financial guidance, and trusted local resources to help you through tough times. Explore free tools that support your well-being.

 

## Trusted guidance when you’re unsure what to do next

Money stress can happen quickly. A delayed payment. A cut in hours. A benefit that doesn’t arrive when you expect it. When that happens, it can feel overwhelming. If this is you today, you’re not alone.

At Numerica, we care about helping you live well, especially when life feels uncertain. 

Here are trusted places to turn when you need support.

## Call 211 for community resources and support

When you’re unsure where to start, 211 is one of the quickest ways to find help.

### What is 211?

211 is a free, nationwide service that connects you with real people trained to match you with resources in your community.

### Who answers the call?

You’ll talk with a local specialist. They listen, ask a few simple questions, and guide you to programs that fit your situation. No judgment. No long hold times. Just help.

### What they can help with?

- Food assistance and meal programs
- Housing and rental resources
- Utility help
- Transportation
- Health and family services
- Local support for seniors, veterans, and caregivers

### How to connect

- Dial 211 from any phone
- Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
- Free and confidential
- Online search available at 211.org

Whether you need food today or just want to understand your options, 211 is a safe place to start.

## Local partners offering food assistance

If you live in Spokane, Tri-Cities, or North Idaho, Second Harvest provides food pantries, mobile markets, and emergency distributions across the region. These resources are free and open to individuals and families.

## Free financial counseling when things feel overwhelming

Money stress can make everything feel heavier. Sometimes talking to someone who understands can help you breathe easier and take the next step.

Through Numerica’s partnership with GreenPath Financial Wellness, you can connect with free, confidential support for:

- Budgeting

GreenPath counselors listen without judgment and help you create a clear path forward.

# Numerica donates $125,000 to help homeless 

Discover how Numerica's $125,000 donation helped families move from shelters into permanent homes during the holidays, creating a brighter future for those in need.

 

Updated Feb. 10, 2022

## Numerica donates $125,000 to give families a home for the holidays

At least 20 individuals and families facing homelessness transitioned out of shelters and into a permanent, stable home this holiday season. A $125,000 donation from Numerica Credit Union funded the effort in partnership with 8 regional nonprofits. This came through Numerica’s Home for the Holidays campaign.

Sarah, a mother of two, lived at Family Promise’s shelter in Spokane for more than a year after escaping domestic violence. She said words could not explain what it means to her family to be in their new home just in time for Christmas.

“It feels amazing, and I feel safe,” Sarah said. “I don’t have to worry about getting kicked out the next day, having food in the fridge, or clean clothes.”

Numerica joined Sarah and her family on their move-in day to watch the credit union’s core purpose of enhancing lives, fulfilling dreams, and building communities come to life.

“Being able to be here and meet with a family whose life has changed for the better is really special,” said Amanda Swan, assistant vice president of Community Development and Impact. “You can instantaneously experience that mission at work and get to see how special this community is. We’re so proud to be able to support families like them.”

The year-end Home for the Holidays gift is allocated to homeless services organizations in Numerica’s four markets:

- Volunteers of America and Family Promise in Spokane
- Vincent de Paul and Safe Passage in North Idaho
- SAGE and Women’s Resource Center in Wenatchee
- Benton-Franklin Community Action Committee and Domestic Violence Services in Tri-Cities

“Without support from organizations like Numerica, nothing happens,” said Larry Riley, executive director of St. Vincent de Paul. “It personifies everything we do. Our mission is to take advantage of every opportunity, so we can help those around us be their best selves going forward. With support from Numerica, we’re able to work together for the betterment of thousands in North Idaho.”

Numerica continued this holiday partnership for a second year after seeing its nonprofit partners respond to growing demands for support services throughout the pandemic. As emergency needs competed for limited funds, moving clients into permanent housing proved to be a struggle. This year’s gift will also support housing stability efforts as nonprofit organizations work to keep vulnerable families from becoming homeless.

“During my 10 years with Numerica, I have been blown away by the generosity of our members giving back to communities in need,” said Carla Cicero, Numerica president and CEO. “I get to see firsthand the impact Numerica’s year-end giving makes when families walk into their new homes.”

SPOKANE, Wash. — Weekend hunger is a significant challenge for many children in the Spokane area, with local food security advocates warning that when school isn't in session, many kids don't have reliable access to meals.

According to Second Harvest Food Bank, approximately one in five children in the region faces daily food insecurity challenges. For these students, school breakfast and lunch programs provide critical nutrition during weekdays, but weekends can leave them vulnerable to hunger.

Today, volunteers from Numerica Credit Union are stepping up to address this need through Second Harvest's Bite-2-Go program. The volunteers will assemble food packages at Second Harvest's facility, preparing them for distribution to local schools.

These weekend food packages will be delivered to schools tomorrow, where they'll be discretely provided to students identified as facing potential weekend hunger. The program's approach ensures students receive the support they need while maintaining their dignity and privacy.

"It's all brand new food. So the kids, it's not donated food or, quote, food bank food. It's purchased brand name food. We care a lot about the kids and their self-worth and their dignity," said Julie Myklebust from Second Harvest Food Bank.

The Bite-2-Go initiative has seen remarkable growth in recent years. "We're in north Idaho. We're in central Washington, we're in the Tri-Cities. We're feeding over 12,000 students per week. So it's grown double, really, since in the last three and a half years, it's doubled," Myklebust explained.

This rapid expansion highlights both the program's success and the persistent challenge of childhood hunger throughout the Inland Northwest region. By providing nutritious, easy-to-prepare food items that children can take home on Fridays, the program helps bridge the weekend meal gap for vulnerable students.

Second Harvest continues to seek community support for this and other food security programs. The organization welcomes both volunteer time and financial contributions to sustain their efforts in combating childhood hunger throughout the region.

Numerica Credit Union is investing more than half a million dollars back into local communities through its annual Numerica Charitable Fund, awarding a record-breaking $532,000 to 23 nonprofit organizations across Eastern Washington and North Idaho. 

Driven by a vision from Numerica President and CEO Carla Cicero to deepen the credit union’s commitment to ending youth poverty, this year marks a historic milestone for the program: for the first time, every nonprofit selected received the full amount it applied for. 

“Through Numerica CARES for Kids, we are serious about ending youth poverty,” said Cicero. “This year, Numerica is investing more action and resources than ever before behind that commitment. These organizations are doing life-changing work every single day by helping families find housing, ensuring children have food to eat, creating educational supports and building brighter futures.” 

Typically, nonprofit organizations submit grant requests that exceed available funding, requiring Numerica to divide the annual charitable fund among recipients. This year, Numerica increased its investment to ensure every selected organization received 100% of its requested funding. 

“We believe in investing in solutions that create lasting impact, and this year we chose to step up in an even bigger way,” said Cicero. Since 2018, the Numerica Charitable Fund has supported more than 100 nonprofits, investing more than $3 million back into Inland Northwest Communities.

SPOKANE, Wash. - Numerica employees dropped off 600 pounds of hygiene products Thursday to Spokane non-profit Project Beauty Share to support the charity's first Hope 4 Kids Hygiene Drive.

4 News Now is partnering with Numerica to collect donations for Project Beauty Share to distribute to nine local school districts.

Numerica has been collecting items at its branches in Spokane and North Idaho and delivered the first round of donations to Project Beauty Share's warehouse.

"These things are definitely important; they help with confidence," said Numerica employee Ashley Overacker. "When you have confidence, you learn better, you grow better and it makes you a better human being. Honestly, it’s a basic human right. They deserve it, we all deserve it."

Project Beauty Share founder and executive director Julie Farley started the drive after hearing from school districts last year.

Kids were coming to school without these basic necessities - or not coming to school because they didn't have things like deodorant and period products.

"The community is so incredible and I think this story really speaks to them," Farley said. "People understand the need for hygiene products and that food stamps don’t cover these items. This is crucial for a student’s self-confidence for them to feel like they can go to school."

The drive continues through October 2.

After donations are collected, they'll be given to students in nine local districts: Medical Lake, Cheney, Spokane Public Schools, Mead, West Valley, East Valley, Central Valley, Post Falls and Coeur d'Alene.

 

 

 

 Melissa Luck, Kirstin O'Connor and Derek Deis from 4 News Now join Numerica Credit Union at the Project Beauty Share warehouse 

The drive got an early boost from deodorant company W by Jake Paul. The company donated four pallets for distribution.

“We’re trying to introduce them to what a typical job would look like,” Hurtado said.

The internship starts with a two-week training, focusing on soft-skills and basic interactions in a job setting. Once the training ends, teens will immerse themselves in a four-week internship, working in different departments at the organization.

“We will have some interns in the childcare area, some in our resource development department, marketing, and there will also be some clerical stuff,” Hurtado said.

This hands-on learning internship gives teens in the community a look at real-world scenarios in the workforce. At the end of their time, each teen will receive a $1,000 stipend.

The program is expected to begin in July, starting with applications and an interview process.

“We are so thankful for Numerica, because they will not only support the teens, but support our vision,” Hurtado said.

### Columbia Basin College Foundation: $25,000

 Columbia Basin College Foundation received $25,000 from Numerica Charitable Fund. Courtesy Numerica Credit Union

Erin Fishburn, executive director of CBC Foundation, said they receive a lot of requests for these kinds of items.

“We started this in January,” Fishburn said. “What we really want to do is support our students so they can stay in school and finish their education.”

Fishburn said the program was surprised to have received the entire amount requested, as grant funding is never guaranteed. They are grateful for the donation as it encourages students to stay in school regardless external factors.

### Communities in Schools of Benton-Franklin: $25,000

 Members from Communities In Schools Benton-Franklin worked to pack spring break care kits for children at Numerica’s activity table during the Tri-City Regional Chamber Annual Meeting and Awards Luncheon event. Courtesy Numerica and CISBF 

This program assigns support coordinators to 28 local schools to help students face challenges outside the classroom that may be preventing them from succeeding. These include food insecurity, housing issues and trauma.

The nonprofit has received this grant from Numerica before, and uses it to fund wraparound support services to students and families, including attendance interventions, mentoring, tutoring, mental health referrals, parent engagement and assistance with basic needs such as housing and food insecurity.

The funding supports the organization’s efforts to connect students and families with resources that address barriers to education and improve academic success.

Lupe Mares-Rojas, executive director of the program, said Numerica has allowed them to achieve their goals as a program.

“They don’t just fund us,” Mares-Rojas said. “They provide our organization with the ongoing support we need to carry out our mission.”

### Lutheran Community Services Northwest: $25,000

 Lutheran Community Services Tri-Cities received $25,000 in funding from Numerica Charitable Fund. Courtesy Numerica Credit Union 

Tri-Cities Lutheran Community Services focuses on children under the age of 21 who are struggling with mental illness and behavioral challenges. They offer services such as counseling, psychiatric evaluations and 24/7 crisis support.

The grant will be used for funding a new youth mental health center in the old Amazon call center, 7011 W. Canal Drive, Kennewick. It will also help to grow their food pantry and meal-kit program, according to Amy Marinoni.

“We serve roughly 400 youth and their families every month,” Marinoni said.

### Safe Harbor Support Center: $20,000

 Safe Harbor Support Center received $20,000 from Numerica Charitable Fund. Courtesy Numerica Credit Union 

Safe Harbor is dedicated to assisting vulnerable youth and families from abuse, trauma and harm in the Tri-Cities. They offer help with basic needs for struggling families, temporary shelters for run-away and homeless youth and mentors for parents navigating the welfare system. This money will be put into continuing all of their current programs.

Sarah Harpster, executive director of Safe Harbor, said they are grateful for Numerica in times when private donations are decreasing.

“We were left speechless,” Harpster said, “They didn’t give us any inclination (that we’d receive the full amount).”

Their programs include housing, meals, clothes, hygiene products and services and other basic needs for youth and families in the Tri-Cities.

## Credit union's emphasis on telling stories leads to more support from its donors

July 30, 2026 Matt Stephens

Consistent donation growth is pushing the Numerica Charitable Fund to new levels as the program has distributed 40% more in grants year over year, totaling a record $532,000 distributed to 23 nonprofits during the 12 months ending in May, Numerica Credit Union data shows.

The Numerica Charitable Fund i s an annual grant program by Numerica Credit Union that invests in regional nonprofits, supporting vulnerable youth and families to address the causes and effects of poverty. Since its launch in 2018, the fund has given over $3 million to local community organizations.

The fund's year-over-year growth is attributed to the credit union's marketing strategies for its charitable giving campaigns, which are focused on a primary mission instead of attempting to support all causes equally, says Amanda Swan, vice president of community impact and communications for the Spokane Valley-based credit union.

"We've been intentional about our focus," Swan says. "When people know what you're trying to accomplish, it's easier for them to become part of that mission."

That concentrated approach has expanded alongside Numerica's charitable investments. The credit union has previously awarded $315,000 through its charitable fund in 2023; $372,000 was awarded in 2024; followed by $380,000 awarded in 2025. 

Grant recipients include Second Harvest Inland Northwest, Family Promise of Spokane, Volunteers of America of Eastern Washington and Northern Idaho, Vanessa Behan, Communities in Schools of Northeast Washington, Boys & Girls Club of Spokane County, Safe Passage, and several other regional nonprofits.

Numerica voluneers sort and pack food donations at Second Harvest Inland Northwest. -Numerica 

Organizations that successfully connect donors with a cause — rather than simply asking for financial support — are often those that help people see themselves in a mission, Swan explains.

"People don't necessarily give because they were asked. They give because they understand why it matters," she says.

That philosophy has helped guide Numerica's charitable efforts through its Numerica CARES for Kids initiative and the Numerica Charitable Fund, which focuses on reducing youth poverty and supporting vulnerable children and families throughout Eastern Washington, North Idaho, the Tri-Cities, and the Wenatchee Valley, she says.

The Numerica Charitable Fund combines contributions from the credit union, its members, and its employees before distributing grants to nonprofit organizations that align with priorities including educational success, financial stability, income and earning potential, and crisis intervention and family stabilization.

Rather than spreading donations across dozens of initiatives, the fund establishes clear allocation priorities that help donors understand exactly where their contributions will be used, Swan contends.

Successful strategies

Successful charitable marketing begins with community awareness before fundraising efforts begin, she says. Organizations first need to educate the public about the problem they are trying to solve because donors are more likely to contribute when they understand both the need and the measurable difference their gifts can make.

That awareness often comes through storytelling.

Instead of leading with statistics alone, organizations should share authentic stories that demonstrate how lives have changed because of community support. Swan says those stories help transform abstract social issues into relatable human experiences.

"When people can picture someone in their own community, maybe even someone who could be their neighbor, the issue becomes real," Swan says.

Emotional storytelling remains one of the strongest drivers of charitable engagement, particularly when paired with transparency and measurable outcomes, Swan says. Donors increasingly expect organizations to demonstrate where money goes, explain how programs operate, and provide evidence of community impact rather than relying solely on emotional appeals, she adds.

Organizations also should think beyond traditional fundraising by helping people understand how financial contributions translate into meaningful outcomes rather than simply emphasizing dollars raised. Blending quantified data with connective storytelling gets the best results, she says.

Campaigns should demonstrate what those dollars accomplish, whether that means providing meals, preventing homelessness, supporting educational achievement, or helping families recover from crises, Swan says.

"It's really about helping people understand the impact behind the investment," Swan says.

Numerica's charitable marketing strategies reflect that philosophy by emphasizing stories from nonprofit partners alongside measurable community outcomes. 

Since launching Numerica CARES for Kids in 2023, the initiative has supported more than 250,000 children and families through food assistance, housing support, school supplies, mentoring, and crisis intervention while investing more than $15 million in communities over the past decade, according data from Numerica. The philanthropic initiative supports over 150 regional nonprofits, sponsors over 150 community events annually, logs over 16,000 yearly volunteer hours, and reports over $1 million in annual giving, Swan says.

Maintaining consistent communication throughout the year instead of only during fundraising campaigns also helps build donor confidence and long-term relationships.

Keeping the public lens pointed at the beneficiary rather than your company is another key strategy, she says.

Messages focused heavily on institutional accomplishments or operational needs often generate less engagement than campaigns highlighting individual stories and community outcomes, and likewise, organizations that overwhelm audiences with statistics or guilt-based messaging can unintentionally discourage participation, Swan explains.

Instead, she recommends presenting a clear problem, illustrating a realistic solution, and showing how every donor can contribute to meaningful change regardless of gift size. She also encourages nonprofits to thank donors, report measurable results, and continue sharing stories after campaigns conclude to reinforce trust and encourage long-term support.

Effective charitable campaigns ultimately succeed because they build new and lasting relationships rather than simple transactions, Swan says.

"When people understand the need, believe in the mission, and can see the impact, they become advocates, not just donors," Swan says.

# Numerica Eliminates Elementary Student Meal Debt

- Posted January 6, 2020

Numerica Credit Union generously donated $1,225.50 to the Wenatchee School District as part of a regional effort to address student lunch debt for low-income elementary students. This holiday season, Numerica contributed a total of $25,000 throughout Spokane, North Idaho, Tri-Cities and Wenatchee to address the growing impact of student lunch debt.

Student lunch debt among Wenatchee School District's seven elementary schools totaled $1,033.13. The remaining $192.37 of donated funds will be applied toward middle school and high school debt, which totals just over $4,300.

"Numerica's generosity will completely erase the elementary debt and pave the way for families to focus on encouraging their children to eat healthy and nutritious meals," said Wenatchee School District nutrition service director Chris Lutgen 

In 2019, four Wenatchee elementary schools (Columbia, Lewis & Clark, Lincoln, and Mission View ) qualified for a federally-funded program that allows all students in those schools to eat breakfast and lunch at no cost. Despite this qualification, students had accumulated negative meal balances from previous years or attended other non-qualified schools and had difficulty paying regular or reduced meal costs. 

The percentage of students eligible for free or reduced lunch under the National School Lunch Program provides a proxy measure for the concentration of low-income students within a school. Wenatchee's School District elementary average free or reduced lunch rate is 61.8 percent. Some schools, such as Columbia and Lincoln Elementary, are over 80 percent. 

"Supporting quality nutrition services and education for our community's children is one way that Numerica fulfills its promise of enhancing lives, fulfilling dreams and building communities," said Kim Pearman-Gillman, SVP of corporate and community relations. "Numerica recognized the burden that student lunch debt can have on families' wellbeing and is proud to help address student lunch debt with a $25,000 investment throughout the region this holiday season."

A check was presented to the District on December 20th at Lincoln Elementary School by Jessica Clay, Numerica's Wenatchee branch Business Development Officer and Andy Stirling SVP of Central Washington Region.

# Local Credit Unions Unite for International Credit Union Day® to Support Tri-Cities Chaplaincy

RICHLAND, WASH. (October 16, 2025) ‒ In celebration of the 77th annual International Credit Union (ICU) Day®, which falls on October 16, five local credit unions – Gesa, HAPO, ICCU, Numerica, and STCU – are partnering with Tri-Cities Chaplaincy to assemble and distribute grief support kits for children and families in need. 

 

Cork’s Place, Tri-Cities Chaplaincy’s children’s grief program, provides these kits as an accessible resource for families who may not be able to attend its physical center. Each kit includes age-appropriate items to help guardians guide children through loss – from journals and memorization tools to books tailored to the type of grief, whether that be from the loss of a parent, sibling or pet. Local schools also rely on the kits to support classrooms impacted by tragedy. In 2025 alone, Cork’s Place distributed more than 400 kits.  

 

As part of this year’s collaboration, credit union team members will volunteer side-by-side to assemble hundreds of kits for future distribution. The credit unions will also pool resources to provide a combined donation of $22,000, ensuring the program can reach even more families across the Tri-Cities.  

 

In addition to building grief kits, volunteers will help set up a series of activity rooms at Cork’s Place designed to help children process grief in safe, accessible, and age-appropriate ways, including: 

 

- Recreation Room: Utilizing a life-size “Grief Jenga and Connect Four” to spark conversations about feelings and coping strategies 
- Art Room: Featuring a “Resilience Shield” activity, where children design shields to represent their strengths 
- Teen Room: Offering a “Grief Monsters” project that helps normalize big emotions through art 
- Paint Splatter Room: Inviting participants to respond to reflective questions through movement and creativity 

 

“At the heart of credit unions is the belief that we make the greatest difference for our communities when we come together.” said Amber Merrill, Community Relations Manager at Gesa Credit Union. “By working with our fellow credit unions to support Tri-Cities Chaplaincy and uplift local families facing hardship, we’re living out the philosophy of ‘people helping people’ in its truest form.” 

 

This International Credit Union Day, the participating credit unions aim to raise awareness about the positive role that credit unions and other financial cooperatives play in their communities and encourage more members to get involved. This year’s theme, “Cooperation for a Prosperous World,” captures the spirit of this work. 

 

International Credit Union Day celebrates the spirit of the global credit union movement. This day is recognized to reflect upon the credit union movement’s history, promote its achievements, recognize its hard work, and share member experiences. International Credit Union Day has been celebrated on the third Thursday of October since 1948.
